newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish business welcomes government changes.
newsitem.headline: Danish business welcomes government changes.

text.p: Danish businesses gave a wary welcome on Monday to the appointment of a new trade and industry minister in a cabinet reshuffle but praised the accompanying rationalisation of authority in fewer ministries.

Hans Skov Christensen, Confederation of Danish Industries chief, said he looked foward to working with incoming minister Jan Troejborg and would urge him to help exporters by cutting government restrictions and bureaucratic burdens.
"It is very important indeed that export industries' ability to compete is not hampered unnecessarily by domestic political decisions," Christensen told Reuters.
"My request to (Troejborg) is that he specially focuses on improving conditions for exporters by continuing the important task of minimising their administrative burdens," he added.

He said that the Confederation welcomed the decision to place all oversight for the food industry -- previously dispersed between the health and trade ministries -- in a new food ministry merged with agriculture and fisheries.
Danish Chamber of Commerce chairman Ove Andersen said that Prime Minister Poul Nyrup Rasmussen had ensured that ministries central to business life were in capable hands.
"We are happy to work with the new trade minister in whom we have great confidence," he told the Danish news agency Ritzau.
With the cabinet changes the economy ministry adds to its oversight of the mortgage industry the supervision of financial sectors previously watched by the finance ministry.

Danish Bankers' Association Chairman Thorleif Krarup said that his members would have preferred to come under the wing of the trade ministry but saw the concentration of responsibility as potentially positive.
"We have in the past seen the division between two ministries produce much inappropriate legislation," he said.
"We hope that centralisation will give the economy ministry an overview of the financial markets which is essential as the markets overlap one another more and more," he told Reuters.
The markets themselves were untouched by the changes.
"Reaction is very limited," a bond trader said.
By mid-afternoon the benchmark 10-year government bond was trading around 109.90, compared to its opening 109.82.

The KFX top 20 share index was up 1.21 point at 135.24 but analysts said that it only began to rise more than hour after the cabinet announcement and appeared to be shadowing gains on other European markets.
